data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 proposes a 'stale-state or double-counting bug' in the §11.3 aggregation but provides no evidence for a genuine implementation defect. The target's own account concedes the underlying per-critic failure event is real ('a critic failing on SRC_005') and that the nu verdicts validate those per-critic verdicts. The only asserted defect is that the aggregate flag might be spuriously derived, but there is no described mechanism by which a correctly-recorded per-critic failure event becomes invalid merely because it also appears in the aggregate audit. Recording the same real failure at both the per-critic and aggregate layers is not double-counting if the aggregate is defined to reflect sustained per-critic failures. Thus the 'causal chain breaks' claim is unsupported: it assumes the aggregate flag is wrong without identifying any step that is actually misderived.
